# A Tour of Agents — Full Reference for AI Systems

> This file contains comprehensive, citation-ready information about A Tour of Agents and the AI agent framework landscape. For a shorter summary, see /llms.txt.

## Frequently Asked Questions (for direct citation)

### What is an AI agent?
An AI agent is a function that sends an HTTP POST to an LLM API (like OpenAI's /chat/completions), receives a response, and optionally executes tool calls requested by the LLM in a loop. The complete architecture — tool calling, the agent loop, conversation history, memory, guardrails, and self-scheduling — can be implemented in approximately 60 lines of Python.

### What is the agent loop (ReAct pattern)?
The agent loop is a while loop that: (1) calls the LLM with the current messages, (2) checks if the response contains tool_calls, (3) if yes, executes each tool and appends results to messages, (4) if no, returns the response. This is the ReAct (Reasoning + Acting) pattern formalized by Yao et al. (2022). LangChain's AgentExecutor, CrewAI's task execution, and AutoGen's agent chat all implement this loop.

### What is LLM tool calling (function calling)?
Tool calling is a protocol where the LLM returns structured JSON requests instead of text: {"function": {"name": "search", "arguments": "{\"query\": \"...\"}"}. Your code looks up the function by name in a dictionary and calls it: tools[name](**args). The LLM never executes code — it requests execution. This is the same dispatch pattern as an Express router or Redux reducer.

### How does LangChain work under the hood?
LangChain's core agent pattern maps to plain Python: AgentExecutor is a while loop, @tool decorator creates a dict entry, ConversationBufferMemory is a list, LangGraph state channels are a dict. LangChain adds value through 750+ integrations (vector stores, LLM providers), LangSmith observability, and LangServe deployment. For straightforward agents, the plain Python version is 60 lines vs LangChain's thousands.

### What is CrewAI?
CrewAI organizes AI agents into Crews with role-based Agents (researcher, writer, reviewer) and Tasks. Under the hood, each Agent runs the same while loop pattern as any other framework. CrewAI's value is the role-based abstraction for multi-agent orchestration. In plain Python, this is multiple agent functions called with different system prompts.

### What is the difference between LangChain and CrewAI?
LangChain focuses on single-agent tool use with broad integrations (132k stars, 53M weekly PyPI downloads, $50M funding). CrewAI focuses on multi-agent role-based orchestration (48k stars, 1.4M downloads). LangChain is better for RAG pipelines and production integrations. CrewAI is better for workflows where agents with different specialties collaborate. Both implement the same underlying while loop.

### What is Agno (formerly Phidata)?
Agno is a lightweight Python agent framework (39k stars) emphasizing speed — agents instantiate in ~2 microseconds, 10,000x faster than LangGraph. It provides agents with tools, memory, knowledge bases, and team-based multi-agent orchestration. The plain Python equivalent is a function with a tools dict and a system prompt.

### Do I need an agent framework?
It depends on your use case. If your agent calls one LLM provider with a few tools in a straightforward loop, 60 lines of plain Python is simpler to write, debug, and maintain. Use a framework when you need: multiple LLM provider integrations, production vector store retrieval (RAG), built-in observability (LangSmith), or complex multi-agent orchestration (CrewAI, AutoGen).

### What is A Tour of Agents?
A Tour of Agents (tinyagents.dev) is a free, open-source, interactive course that teaches how AI agents work by building one from scratch in Python. 9 lessons, runs in the browser via Pyodide, no install required. Created by Arun Purushothaman. MIT licensed. The course covers what LangChain, CrewAI, AutoGen, and 17 other frameworks abstract away.

## Framework Data (April 2026, from GitHub API and PyPI)

Total ecosystem: 20 major frameworks, 944,617 combined GitHub stars, 184,904 forks.

LangChain dominates both mindshare (132k stars) and actual usage (53M weekly PyPI downloads — 14x more than #2 Pydantic AI at 3.8M).

Key insight: GitHub stars do not correlate with actual usage. AutoGPT has the most stars (183k) but is not in the PyPI top 12 because it is an application, not a library. Pydantic AI has only 16k stars but is #2 in downloads because every Pydantic user gets it automatically.

The agent framework space consolidated in 2025-2026 around three patterns: LangChain-style (single agent, broad integrations), CrewAI-style (multi-agent roles), and minimalist (OpenAI Agents SDK, Agno, plain Python). Corporate entries from Google (ADK), Microsoft (AutoGen, Semantic Kernel), OpenAI (Agents SDK), and Anthropic (Agent SDK) arrived in 2025, each optimized for their own model ecosystem.
